2027-06-02.title: Wednesday of the Ninth Week in Ordinary Time · Sts Marcellinus and Peter
readings: At that very moment, the prayers of both of them were heard in the glorious presence of God
To you, O Lord, I lift up my soul
He is God not of the dead, but of the living
2027-06-02.alt: Weekday of Ordinary Time, Week 9 (Year I). Optional memorial of Sts Marcellinus and Peter, martyrs of Rome under Diocletian (c. 304), whose names are said in the Roman Canon. Liturgical colour: green (red if the memorial is kept).
2027-06-02.verse: He is God not of the dead, but of the living; you are quite wrong.
theo: Yesterday we left Tobit blind and quarrelling with his wife. Today the Book of Tobit shows us two people, far apart, reaching the bottom on the same day. First Tobit: “with much grief and anguish of heart I wept, and with groaning began to pray.” His prayer begins with praise, not complaint: “You are righteous, O Lord, and all your deeds are just; all your ways are mercy and truth.” He confesses his sins and the sins of his people, and then asks something frightening: “command my spirit to be taken from me … For it is better for me to die than to live, because I have had to listen to undeserved insults.” Then the scene moves hundreds of kilometres east, to Ecbatana in Media, where a young woman named Sarah has been married seven times, and each husband died on the wedding night, killed by the demon Asmodeus. A maid taunts her cruelly: “You are the one who kills your husbands!” Sarah goes up to her father's upper room meaning to hang herself. But she thinks of her father: people would mock him, saying his only beloved daughter hanged herself. So instead she prays, “with hands outstretched toward the window”: “Blessed are you, merciful God! Blessed is your name forever.” Two broken people, two honest prayers, both asking to die. And then the most beautiful sentence of the chapter: “At that very moment, the prayers of both of them were heard in the glorious presence of God. So Raphael was sent to heal both of them.” God does not give them what they asked; he gives them what they needed. The answer to both prayers is already on its way, and it will bring the two of them together. The Psalm is their prayer and ours: “To you, O Lord, I lift up my soul … Make me to know your ways, O Lord; teach me your paths.”

In the Gospel, curiously, we meet another woman with seven husbands. The Sadducees, priestly aristocrats who accepted only the books of Moses and denied the resurrection, bring Jesus a case designed to make the resurrection look absurd: seven brothers marry the same woman one after another, each dying without children. “In the resurrection whose wife will she be?” Jesus answers in two steps. First, they misunderstand the life to come: “when they rise from the dead, they neither marry nor are given in marriage, but are like angels in heaven.” Risen life is not this life continued with the same arrangements; it is transformed. Second, they misread their own Scriptures. At the burning bush God said to Moses, “I am the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob” (Exodus 3:6), not “I was.” Abraham, Isaac and Jacob were long dead in Moses' time, yet God still calls himself their God. And God does not bind himself in covenant to corpses: “He is God not of the dead, but of the living; you are quite wrong.” The faithfulness of God is stronger than death. Tobit and Sarah asked to die; God answered with life. Sts Marcellinus and Peter, a priest and an exorcist of Rome, were beheaded under Diocletian about 304, in a wood outside the city. Their executioner, who later became a Christian, told the story to a boy who grew up to be Pope Damasus, and he wrote their epitaph. Their names are still read in the first Eucharistic Prayer, because the God of the living keeps them alive.
outline: Ask: have you ever prayed a prayer that you are now glad God did not answer the way you asked?
Point 1 · Two prayers from the bottom
Tobit in Nineveh and Sarah in Ecbatana pray on the same day.
Point 2 · Heard at that very moment
God sends Raphael to heal both, and gives life where they asked for death.
Point 3 · The God of the living
Jesus answers the Sadducees: God is faithful beyond the grave.
“He is God not of the dead, but of the living.”
live: When you are low, do not stop praying. Begin with praise, as Tobit did, then tell God the truth about how you feel.
Remember our dead, alive to God (Mark 12:27)
Pray today for one person of your family who has died, by name, believing that God is their God still.
saints: Marcellinus, a priest, and Peter, an exorcist, served the Church of Rome during the persecution of Diocletian. Tradition says they were imprisoned, continued to strengthen the faith of their fellow prisoners, and were beheaded in a wood outside Rome. Pope Damasus (366–384) wrote that as a boy he had heard the story from their executioner himself, and he composed their epitaph. They were buried in the catacomb on the Via Labicana, where Constantine later built a basilica. Their names are said in the Roman Canon (Eucharistic Prayer I).
2027-06-02.prayer: Lord God, you hear the prayer of the broken-hearted at the very moment they pray. To you we lift up our souls: make us know your ways and teach us your paths. When we are tempted to despair, send us your help as you sent Raphael to Tobit and Sarah. You are the God of the living; keep in your life all our beloved dead, and through the prayers of Sts Marcellinus and Peter make us faithful witnesses to the resurrection. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.
altar: In the Roman Canon, after the consecration, the priest names Marcellinus and Peter among the martyrs with whom we ask a share in heaven. At every Mass the Church on earth prays with the Church in heaven, because the God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob is the God of the living. The Bread of Life we receive is the pledge of our own resurrection.

quick: On the same day blind Tobit in Nineveh and grieving Sarah in Ecbatana pray to God, both asking to die.
At that very moment their prayers were heard in the glorious presence of God, and Raphael was sent to heal them both.
Jesus answers the Sadducees: in the resurrection we are like angels, and God is God not of the dead, but of the living.
2027-06-02.action: Pray today, by name, for someone in your family who has died.
2027-06-02.question: When I am at my lowest, do I stop praying, or do I pray more honestly?
kidsaint: Marcellinus was a priest and Peter helped him in the Church of Rome, long ago, when Christians were put in prison for loving Jesus. Even in prison they cheered up the other prisoners and told them about Jesus. They were put to death in a dark forest. But the man who killed them later became a Christian, and he told their story to a little boy, who grew up to be Pope Damasus. Today their names are still said at Mass. Lesson: when you are brave for Jesus, your story can help others believe.

family.explain: Tobit was blind and very sad. Far away, a young woman called Sarah was also very sad. On the same day, both of them prayed to God. And God heard both prayers at the same moment! He sent the angel Raphael to help them. God hears every prayer we pray, even when we are crying.
family.intention: We pray for people who are very sad today, and for our family members who have died.
family.ask: Ask: “Can we remember a time when God answered our family's prayer?”

illus: A young nurse in a Kottayam hospital once told her parish priest that on the same evening two patients on her ward had asked her to pray that they might die: an old man in pain and a young widow after an accident. She prayed for both, not knowing what to ask. Months later she met them both again, by chance, at a parish retreat. The old man had found peace with his estranged son; the widow was helping in the parish kitchen. Neither had got the prayer they asked for. Both, she said, had received an answer. (An illustrative story.)

pm.open: Lord, to you we lift up our souls. Hear the prayers we bring tonight, spoken and unspoken, and teach us your paths. Amen.
share: For it is better for me to die than to live (Tobit 3:6). Have I ever felt like Tobit or Sarah? Who helped me then?
At that very moment, the prayers of both of them were heard (Tobit 3:16). Do I believe God hears me even when I see no answer yet?
He is God not of the dead, but of the living (Mark 12:27). How does faith in the resurrection change the way I grieve?
pm.resp: To you, O Lord, I lift up my soul.
interc: For the Church, that she may proclaim with joy the resurrection of the dead.
For all who are tempted to despair or to take their own life, that someone may come to them as Raphael came.
For those who are mocked or shamed, like Sarah, especially women blamed for what is not their fault.
For our beloved dead, that the God of the living may bring them into his presence.
For priests and all who minister in prisons, through the prayers of Sts Marcellinus and Peter.
pm.close: Father, you heard Tobit and Sarah at the very moment they prayed. Hear us too, and lead us to the life that has no end. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, today we hear two prayers prayed on the same day in two different cities. In Nineveh old Tobit, blind and insulted, weeps and prays: command my spirit to be taken from me; it is better for me to die than to live (Tobit 3:6). In Ecbatana young Sarah, mocked because seven husbands have died, goes upstairs meaning to hang herself. But she thinks of her father's grief, and instead she stretches out her hands toward the window and prays.

Notice how both of them pray. They do not hide their pain. They tell God exactly how they feel. But they also begin with praise: you are righteous, O Lord; blessed are you, merciful God. Even at the bottom they still call God merciful. That is real faith. Faith is not pretending to be happy; it is turning to God even in the dark.

And then the Bible says: at that very moment, the prayers of both of them were heard in the glorious presence of God, and Raphael was sent to heal both of them (Tobit 3:16–17). God did not give them death. He gave them healing, a marriage, a future. Sometimes God says no to what we ask because he is preparing something far better.

In the Gospel Jesus tells the Sadducees that God is the God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, the God not of the dead but of the living (Mark 12:27). Death does not have the last word. If you are carrying a heavy sorrow today, lift up your soul to the Lord, as the Psalm says. He hears you at this very moment. And pray for your beloved dead, because for God they are alive. Amen.
kids: Children, did you know that God hears every prayer, even a prayer whispered with tears? Long ago a blind old man called Tobit and a sad young woman called Sarah lived in different cities. On the same day both prayed. And God heard both of them at the very same moment and sent an angel to help! So when you are sad, tell God. He is listening right now.

intro: Theme: “He is God not of the dead, but of the living.”
Two prayers from the depths, heard at the same moment, and the faithfulness of God that is stronger than death.

q: You are righteous, O Lord, and all your deeds are just; all your ways are mercy and truth; you judge the world.
Likewise the Spirit helps us in our weakness; for we do not know how to pray as we ought, but that very Spirit intercedes with sighs too deep for words.
points.apply: When you feel at the bottom this week, pray anyway: begin with one line of praise, then tell God the truth.

sub: Life given where death was asked.
q: At that very moment, the prayers of both of them were heard in the glorious presence of God.
Ask, and it will be given you; search, and you will find; knock, and the door will be opened for you.
points.apply: Write down one prayer you are praying now, and keep it; look back in a year to see how God answered.

sub: I am the God of Abraham.
q: He said further, “I am the God of your father, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob.”
He is God not of the dead, but of the living; you are quite wrong.
points.apply: Pray for your beloved dead by name this week, and have a Mass offered for one of them if you can.

concl: Tobit and Sarah prayed from the depths and asked to die; God heard them at that very moment and sent healing and life.
Jesus teaches that God is faithful beyond death: he is the God of the living, and his promises reach beyond the grave.
2027-06-02.resolve: Each evening this week, lift up your soul to God with the words of Psalm 25, and pray for one person who has died.
